ust.method: Overnight = New York closes strictly before each Jakarta close (New York shuts at about 04:00–05:00 Jakarta). Hedged = INDOGB 10Y minus β × US 10Y, β the trailing 26-week weekly beta known at the time. All variants walk-forward, z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks, thresholds ±0.5, hit rates over the next 4 weeks. The 'Beta 3Y' slot carries the INDOGB 15Y.

src: Yahoo Finance: IDX Composite (^JKSE) and USD/IDR (IDR=X) daily closes; any USD/IDR close more than 1.5% from Bank Indonesia’s JISDOR fix is replaced by JISDOR. INDOGB 10Y: PHEI IGSYC (CNBC benchmark 10Y before the first stored PHEI day). US Treasury daily par yields (2Y, 10Y; home.treasury.gov). Weekly, last trading day of each week.

method.window: 4-week changes; z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks (min 26); thresholds ±0.5

method.window: 20-day changes; z-scores vs trailing 260 sessions (min 130); spread vs its 130-day average; thresholds ±0.5; hit rates over the next 20 sessions; UST hedge β = trailing 130-day daily beta
components: INDOGB − UST 10Y spread vs its 130-day average (wide = cheap)

notes.headline: Asia's tech rout skipped Jakarta: JCI +0.4% with Rp328bn of foreign equity buying and JISDOR steady at 18,130, but the 10Y INDOGB holds 7.70%, 47bp higher in four weeks and mostly not explained by Treasuries. Signal −0.94: bond sell-off
notes.now: Foreign money is still out of Indonesian stocks over the month, but Friday showed some resilience. A US tech sell-off took the Kospi down 8% at the open; the JCI fell 2% in the morning yet closed 0.4% higher at 5,050 with foreigners net buyers of Rp328bn (who bought is not disclosed). It is still 21% down over 20 sessions, and the rupiah is 1.6% weaker over the same span (JISDOR 18,130; spot 18,089) even as FX reserves rose $0.5bn to $146.8bn. Bonds have paid through price: the 10Y INDOGB is up 70bp over 20 sessions to 7.70%, though the 2–4Y sector fell 6–8bp today. Three of the four signal parts point to a sell-off (JCI z −2.32, rupiah z +0.55, 10Y trend z +2.60), and only the spread part is bond-bullish: INDOGBs pay 286bp over Treasuries, 46bp above their 130-day average (z +1.70) and a new 52-week high; the daily signal is −0.94 (−0.86 on Thursday). Treasuries explain little of the trend: the US 10Y fell 38bp in four weeks and the 26-week weekly beta is −0.21, so about +8bp of the 47bp four-week rise is the Treasury-linked part and +39bp is residual, which is what the US move does not explain rather than proof of domestic selling or political risk. On the day the link broke: Thursday's 5.5bp New York rally implied about −1.9bp for INDOGBs at the 1-year daily beta of 0.34, yet the 10Y moved −0.1bp; INDOGBs follow large US moves in the same direction about 73% of the time, smaller ones much less reliably. The signal has read sell-off since Oct 7 and the 10Y is 54bp higher since, a hit for this episode. Its record on the daily build since June 2022 is a Sharpe of 0.77 outright and 0.90 hedged against Treasuries, with sell-off calls right 51% and rally calls 58% over the next 20 sessions; these are in-sample back-tests. Our read for the next 2–4 weeks: stay underweight duration until BI acts or the rupiah holds below 18,100 for a week; with the spread cushion at its widest of the year, the turn could be fast when it comes.
notes.flip: The daily signal returns to neutral above −0.5: roughly, the JCI 4-week return back above −5% or the 10Y's 4-week rise slowing below 20bp, with USD/IDR flat or lower. A move to bond rally (above +0.5) needs a JCI rebound and a firmer rupiah together, the pattern that started the April 2025 rally. The policy triggers are a BI-Rate hike that steadies the rupiah (bearish for the front end on the day, bullish for the trend after) or MSCI softening its Standalone proposal.
phases: JCI 6,500–7,250 while the 10Y rose from 6.2% to a 7.58% peak in October 2022 as global rates surged; stocks held up on the commodity boom.
JCI 6,630–7,380 and 10Y 6.19–7.21%. Stocks and bonds drifted without a clear link, and the signal's calls lost money (Sharpe −0.3 from 2022 to August 2024).
JCI fell from 7,812 to 6,258 while the 10Y rose from 6.43% to 7.19%: stocks, rupiah and bonds sold off together, the pattern the signal is built for. Its record improves sharply from here.
JCI climbed from 6,262 to a record 9,075 on Jan 15, 2026, and the 10Y fell to 5.93% in October 2025 as foreign money returned and BI eased.

MSCI froze Indonesian index changes in January and on Oct 15 proposed Standalone status; BI hiked 100bp to 5.75% by June and now weighs more, while a wiretapping case against senior police officers adds political risk. JCI −44% to about 5,050, 10Y up 159bp to 7.70%: the second and deeper foreign exit, though foreigners still bought SBN in October.
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows: daily foreign SBN holdings (DJPPR) and equity flows (IDX) are not machine-readable for the dashboard, so the rupiah and the JCI stand in for foreign money, and any statement about who bought or sold is a hypothesis. USD/IDR is Yahoo's close, replaced by Bank Indonesia's JISDOR fix on any day it strays more than 1.5% (Yahoo printed ~17,480 from Nov 3, 2026 while JISDOR was ~18,100). Before Oct 29, 2026 the 10Y is CNBC's benchmark-bond yield rather than PHEI's IGSYC, with repeated stale prints removed. The daily back-test runs from June 2022 (958 sessions): the live signal makes 195bp outright (Sharpe 0.77) and 224bp hedged against Treasuries (Sharpe 0.90), against −32bp for always holding the 10Y; the weekly build scores 0.33 and 0.45. Variants that use the US 10Y trend score up to 0.78 on the weekly build but were picked after the fact and are not live. In-sample, no trading costs; not a trading system.
